newsitem.title: UK: Kvaerner to beef up units' performances.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner to beef up units' performances.

text.p: Erik Tonseth, president and chief executive of Norwegian shipbuilding and engineering group Kvaerner, said on Monday the group was taking steps to improve its businesses' performance.
"This year's aggregated results for the Kvaerner group are not satisfactory. But we are taking firm action to improve the performances of those businesses which are under-performing," Tonseth said.
Progress towards getting the most from the integration of its global contracting operations should result in savings of more than 200 million annually, the company said.

Kvaerner also said that the formation of a new headquarters structure will result in an annual cost savings of around 200 million crowns. The firm has reduced its corporate staff and will shortly relocate to another company site on the outskirts of Oslo.
The Norwegian group revealed earlier that pretax profits slipped to 851 million Norwegian crowns for the nine months to September 30.
The company said this compared with 1.9 billion crowns for the same period in 1995. Analysts' forecasts had centred on pre-tax profits of around 847 million crowns.
Operating profits at Kvaerner decreased by 747 million Norwegian crowns to 912 million, while earnings per share slipped to 32.13 crowns from 14.17 previously.

The results include five months operations from British conglomerate Trafalgar House, which Kvaerner acquired in April, and a 258 million crowns profit from the sale of ships compared with 568 million previously. The sale of other assets also realised 468 million crowns.
Kvaerner said that 1995 results included a gain of 219 million crowns on discontinued gas shipping operations and foreign exchange earnings.
